questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The University of Milan offered courses that aligned well with my studies in Communication and IT, particularly within communication, organisation, and technology. In addition, the opportunity to study in an international academic environment and to experience everyday life and culture in Italy was an important factor, as I wanted to challenge myself both academically and personally.

questions.answer: Overall, it was relatively easy to find the necessary information upon arrival. The host university provided relevant information in advance and upon arrival, which helped with practical matters such as enrolment, course registration and access to university systems

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding off-campus housing required some effort and planning, as the housing market in Milan is competitive. Starting the search early and using multiple platforms was helpful.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is recommended to verify listings carefully, be cautious of scams, and consider temporary accommodation initially while searching for a more permanent place.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Overall, I was successful in registering for the classes I had planned. While some adjustments were necessary due to availability and scheduling, I was able to enrol in relevant courses that aligned well with my academic objectives.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is helpful to have a flexible course plan in case adjustments are needed due to availability.

questions.answer: BA

questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the academic level was manageable and intellectually stimulating. But the MA courses were difficult, since I am on my bachelor.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at the host institution differed from that of UCPH in that it was generally more lecture-based and instructor-centred. At UCPH, there is typically a stronger emphasis on student participation, discussion and critical engagement.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Traveling in Italy, exploring the city and surrounding regions, engaging in cultural activities such as visiting museums and exhibitions, and experiencing local food culture are also highly recommended.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Lake Como and going to art museums.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Overall, it was relatively easy to adjust to the local culture. The environment was welcoming, and everyday interactions helped facilitate the adaptation process.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would recommend actively participating in classes, group work and student activities, as this provides natural opportunities to meet local students. Being open, showing interest in the local culture and making an effort to communicate in the local language can also help. Additionally, joining social events or informal gatherings organised by the university or student groups can make it easier to build connections.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One of the more challenging cultural differences was the more flexible approach to time and organisation compared to what I am used to at UCPH. Administrative processes and communication could sometimes take longer, and schedules were occasionally less predictable. However, adapting to this difference also encouraged greater flexibility and patience, and it became easier over time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The appreciation of culture, history and food

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was the opportunity to develop both academically and personally in an international environment. Engaging with different perspectives, academic traditions and cultures broadened my understanding of my field of study. At the same time, living abroad strengthened my independence, adaptability and confidence, making the overall experience highly valuable.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during the exchange was adapting to the exam formats and assessment methods at the host institution. The structure, expectations and evaluation criteria differed from those at my home institution, which required adjustment and careful preparation.
